Hi Lara / Ethan —

Following up on our MAP workshop this morning. Per the action items, we want to lock the unit-econ inputs so procurement can draft terms and our infra team can validate capacity. Key items we need from your side (short answers are fine):

- Average conversational session length (avg user turns): what are you seeing in production for the pilot cohort?
- Typical prompt + response token breakdown (approx): tokens in -> tokens out
- Percent of requests that can be served from a short-term prefix cache (e.g., canned replies / known intents)
- Peak concurrent sessions expected during weekday peak (PST) and acceptable tail latency (p95/p99)

We attached the traffic-profiles CSV with the format we're using for the MAP econ model. If you can fill the highlighted columns (traffic shape, avg tokens in/out, cacheable share), we’ll run a sensitivity sim and push a final units-per-dollar table into the MAP draft.

Also: to be transparent about assumptions on our side — for the pilot we’re modeling: 8-bit quantized variants when appropriate, automatic batching with 50–200ms aggregation windows (depending on latency SLO), and prefix KV caching for recurrent templates. We’ll call out a fallback model (smaller context / cheaper variant) if concurrency spikes.

Next steps: if you can return the CSV by EOD Friday (2025-05-09), we can have a finalized econ appendix for the MAP and a short ops playbook for the pilot.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

- Avg session turns (pilot cohort): 5.2 turns per session (includes follow-ups).
- Token breakdown (avg): ~60 tokens in -> ~180 tokens out (we use a templated response expansion for summaries).

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Lara — the numbers are helpful. A couple of points from pricing/close perspective: 

- We will produce the units-per-dollar table with three scenarios: conservative (no prefix caching, single-model full precision), baseline (your reported cacheable share + 8-bit quantization where quality tolerates), and aggressive (prefetching + higher batching targets).
- Procurement requested both a monthly committed units schedule and an on-demand fallback rate. I'll loop in legal on the SLA language we discussed.
- For the MAP appendix, please flag which intents are absolutely non-cacheable (PHI-sensitive flows) so we can exclude them from caching assumptions in the conservative column.

Operational ask for engineering: Karthik, can you confirm whether our batching window at 50–200ms with a 128 max batch size aligns with the p99 target of 1.8s for Clarion? If not, propose adjustments (smaller batch size, lower aggregation time, or preferded fallback model).

Subject: Re: MAP: unit economics reconciliation & caching/batching assumptions

Thanks — quick engineering readout. Summary first, details below:

- Short answer: yes, 50–200ms aggregation windows with max batch ~128 are workable, but to reliably hit p99=1.8s at 310 concurrent sessions we recommend: target batching window 80ms, dynamic batch sizing with a hard timeout of 200ms, and an autoscale policy that spins one extra worker per 250 concurrent sessions during pilot ramp.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache at the routing layer will reduce token spend for cacheable templates by ~85% (since we avoid full forward). We recommend pinning the top-25 templates for warm cache and a small TTL (60s) for others during peak.
- Quantization: 8-bit variants for non-latency-sensitive intents are fine; for summary-generation paths where quality matters we keep fp16. That mix maps to an expected tokens-per-dollar improvement of ~2.3x in baseline vs. full-precision.

Operational checklist (for the MAP appendix):
1) Confirm list of non-cacheable intents (Lara) — we’ll publish conservative econ column with those excluded.
2) We’ll run a 2-hour synthetic ramp using Clarion’s provided traffic profile (Olga to coordinate test window). Output: tokens/sec, avg token latency, batch distribution.
3) Post-test, we’ll produce a short one-page ops playbook: expected cold-cache ramp, emergency fallback routing (smaller model variant), and who to loop for infra scale (on-call + CSM).

I’ll push a draft units-per-dollar CSV to the drive link by EOD Monday. If procurement needs an explicit cost table in the SOW, Ben — we can produce both a sample committed schedule and an on-demand price sheet.

-Karthik
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
